industrial_problem: Unsafe autonomous tool execution causes duplicate side effects, unauthorized actions, or corrupted business state
buyer_or_user: Platform engineering, AI infrastructure, operations, security, compliance
why_business_cares: Agents now call APIs, update databases, send emails, create tickets, and modify external systems; a wrong or repeated tool call can create real operational damage
evidence_signal: Very high: 562 tool-calling issue hits and 355 reliability issue hits
current_workaround: Tool schemas, retries, max-iteration limits, approval gates, guardrails, logs
remaining_gap: Current systems validate tool-call format more than whether the action is necessary, reversible, authorized, and causally useful
research_angle: State-transition-conditioned tool selection and state-delta validation for agent actions
hackathon_fit: Excellent: small runtime layer around Qwen-Agent, measurable demo, clear before/after baseline

industrial_problem: Agent governance is too coarse for production workflows
buyer_or_user: Security, compliance, enterprise architecture, platform teams
why_business_cares: Enterprises need traceable, policy-compliant agent actions across tools, users, and teams; shadow agents and weak guardrails increase audit and data-exposure risk
research_angle: Manual approval, static allowlists, human review, generic guardrails
hackathon_fit: Approval is treated as binary instead of risk-budgeted; governance is often bolted on after the agent chooses an action
representative_sources: Risk-scored action approval and auditable action receipts
column11: Strong: can demo with payment/email/CRM mock actions and approval thresholds

industrial_problem: Blind retries and long-running agent loops amplify failures
buyer_or_user: Platform engineering, SRE, workflow automation teams
why_business_cares: Retries that help normal software can duplicate side effects, burn tokens, create inconsistent state, and hide root causes in agent systems
evidence_signal: Very high: 1066 combined evidence signal for tool loops and failed termination
current_workaround: Retry policies, checkpointing, recursion limits, timeouts, manual inspection
remaining_gap: Agents often detect failure only after repeated actions, not by measuring lack of progress after each tool call
research_angle: Non-progress detector for tool-use trajectories with repair or escalation
hackathon_fit: Excellent: easy to show loop baseline versus monitored agent

industrial_problem: Agent evaluation does not match industrial success criteria
buyer_or_user: Product owners, AI platform teams, QA, customer operations
why_business_cares: A demo can look successful while failing domain policy, database state, consistency, or user satisfaction under repeated trials
remaining_gap: Traces, unit tests, LLM-as-judge, manual review, task-specific evals
research_angle: Many evals inspect outputs or traces, while industry needs final-state correctness, policy compliance, and reliability across repeated runs
hackathon_fit: State-based evaluation harness for tool agents
representative_sources: Strong: useful as benchmark layer, but less flashy than runtime control

industrial_problem: Agent memory and context can inject unsafe or stale operational facts
buyer_or_user: Security, platform engineering, knowledge management, customer support
why_business_cares: Memory poisoning, stale account facts, and untrusted retrieved content can steer later actions in business workflows
research_angle: Vector search, summaries, memory stores, prompt filters, retrieval policies
hackathon_fit: Memory is often optimized for relevance, not trust, freshness, contradiction risk, or action impact
representative_sources: Decision-impact memory gate with trust and freshness scoring
column11: Good: more research novelty, but evaluation is harder in 10-12 days
